Q: Do I learn React before JavaScript? I'm confused A:

You should learn JavaScript first. React is built on top of JavaScript, so without the basics (variables, functions, arrays, ES6 features) React will feel confusing. Once you’re comfortable with JavaScript, React will be much easier to pick up.

Q: Could not initialize Xv output A:

Hm do you have libxv somewhere? Find what happens when you check gst-inspect-1.0 xvimagesink ? Also there is library path mentioned (| grep Filename).. you can ldd it:

ldd /usr/local/lib/gstreamer-1.0/libgstxvimagesink.so

I had some problems with this as well.. try to install libxv-dev or libxv1.. maybe dev is safer.

Q: How to change the connections in SSIS package after deployment? A:

once you have deployed your package navigate to Integration Services Catalog -> SSISDB -> your SSIS Project. Once there open up the desired package and under [Connections] tab you can change the connection. Alternative to this (method 2) is to create Environments; where you can quickly change between dev, qa, prod by checking towards the bottom which environment you wish SSIS to pick up config from.

Q: .NETFramework,Version=v4.5 framework is a higher version than the currently targeted framework ".NETFramework,Version=v3.5" A:

It appears that your second project is not targeting the .net 4.5 framework. You can right click your second project and go to properties ->Application.

It will say target framework is 3.5, change that to 4.5 and make sure this is also the case for your first project as well

Q: Woocommerce show shipping methods in checkout page? A:

This Worked for me:

Under WooCommerce/Settings/Shipping zones clear the 'Zone regions' then under shipping options/ Calculations uncheck both:

  1. "Enable the shipping calculator on the cart page" and
  2. "Hide shipping costs until an address is entered"

The plugin
"Shipping Method Display Style for WooCommerce" by "Thedotstore" may be handy.

Q: the usefulness of await on my async login method A:

You are using await at two place in your code.

await bcrypt.compare(password,user.password)

The compare function will execute asynchronously to avoid blocking event loop, and return promise in pending state if you do not use await keyword here. If you want to synchronously compare password, you can use bcrypt.compareSync(password,user.password) , but this will block the event loop for some seconds.

const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({where:{email:email}})

You need to use the await keyword here, because findUnique executes asynchronously and return promise.

You can read more about await from MDN docs
